morning_soundtrack.title: Wilco & Billy Bragg’s Mermaid Avenue: The Complete Sessions Gets More Complete With Expanded New Box Set
morning_soundtrack.snippet: In 1998, between their first masterpiece Being There and their next masterpiece Summerteeth , Wilco teamed up with the English folksinger Billy Bragg to release Mermaid Avenue , a batch of newly written songs built from old unused Woody Guthrie lyrics. It's where Wilco got "California Stars," a perennial live staple, and they followed it up in 2000 with Mermaid Ave. Vol. II .
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like finding a handwritten letter tucked inside a secondhand book — history made warm and immediate by people who genuinely loved it.

morning_soundtrack.title: Gay Meat – “Leslie”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: In April, North Carolina's Karl Kuehn, who records under the moniker Gay Meat, released his debut album Blue Water . The project is a loving reflection of passing time and the increasing weight of impending grief. On Wednesday, Gay Meat returned with "Leslie," a new song that was written for Blue Water but didn't make the final cut.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The kind of song you put on when you're finally ready to feel the thing you've been quietly avoiding all week.

morning_soundtrack.title: Weathering The Storm With Johnny Blue Skies & The Dark Clouds
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Johnny Blue Skies & The Dark Clouds entered the stage to the sound of a heavy descending guitar riff like something out of a doom metal track. Then the disco ball turned on, and Sturgill Simpson started playing a smoky blues guitar solo over jazz chords. The introduction then resolved in the funky syncopated groove of “Venus,” which was soon graced by the hearty twang of Simpson’s voice, country to the bone.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: A sweaty, smoky bar where the jukebox refuses to be put in a box and neither does the man on stage.

morning_soundtrack.title: David Byrne and Daniel Pemberton Made a Song Using Weird Elon Musk Quotes
morning_soundtrack.snippet: “Let Me Sell You a Dream” appears in Musk, a new documentary about the tech mogul directed by Alex Gibney
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The art-rock equivalent of watching a magician pull absurdity out of a silicon-valley-shaped hat.

morning_soundtrack.title: Andrew Savage Launches New Band Iconic Fugues With “2025 Dream/2025 Blues”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: “I think it’s just amazing the way a fun guitar solo can draw a bit of sun out from behind the clouds”
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: That specific relief of a guitar solo breaking through a grey mood like the first genuinely warm day of March.

morning_soundtrack.title: Emily A. Sprague :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
morning_soundtrack.snippet: In an album as lyrically economic as the startlingly beautiful Cyano , the latest solo release from Emily A. Sprague—familiar to many as the thoughtful anchor of indie-folk outfit Florist—even the few words we’re given can feel like lifelines. “We have to take care of ourselves” is one such arresting declaration. That reminder of self-preservation runs through Sprague’s ethereal ambient work, where emotion is conveyed less through narrative or explanation than through the feeling embedded in her evocative melodies.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Music that feels like standing very still in a forest and realizing the silence itself is saying something.

morning_soundtrack.title: Loretta Lynn’s Jack White-Produced Album Van Lear Rose Is Finally Returning to Streaming
morning_soundtrack.snippet: After being mysteriously pulled from streaming services in 2021, the Grammy-winning album is finally returning in both digital and physical formats. Loretta Lynn’s Jack White-Produced Album Van Lear Rose Is Finally Returning to Streaming Jonah Krueger
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Dust-and-diesel Appalachian thunder that sounds like it was always meant to be played too loud in a pickup truck.

morning_soundtrack.title: City of Los Angeles to Declare “Billy Idol Day” on November 13th
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The legendary rocker and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens will both be honored. City of Los Angeles to Declare “Billy Idol Day” on November 13th Spencer Kaufman
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Pure leather-jacket nostalgia for an era when rock stars were basically municipal monuments anyway.

morning_soundtrack.title: Guns N’ Roses Added to Aerosmith’s Upcoming Comeback Shows
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The concerts are taking place October 29th and November 1st at the Hollywood Bowl. Guns N’ Roses Added to Aerosmith’s Upcoming Comeback Shows Spencer Kaufman
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The Hollywood Bowl about to shake loose its bolts for one gloriously excessive night of arena-rock excess.

morning_soundtrack.title: And Away We Go: Jackie Gleason, Jazz and the Music for Lovers Only LP Series
morning_soundtrack.snippet: T he legendary comedian and actor Jackie Gleason often listed “musician,” “composer” and “conductor” as a part of his official biography, but in truth he …
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Candlelit and unhurried, like slow-dancing in a hotel ballroom long after everyone else has gone to bed.

morning_soundtrack.title: Duane Betts Blazes a Fresh Trail on the Isle of Hope Tour
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Duane Betts' sound conjures a musical sanctuary, highlighted in a festive two-night stand at the Bay Area's Sweetwater Music Hall.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Warm Southern-rock comfort food served on a breezy California evening with a cold drink in hand.

morning_soundtrack.title: Embla and the Karidotters Subvert Country Music Conventions
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Norway's "queer country" Embla and the Karidotters deliver high-energy fun performed by a kick-ass, live-show-honed band, anchored by strong songs.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: A barn dance that blew its own walls out and invited everyone who was never supposed to be there.

global_silver_linings.title: Good News in History, October 9
global_silver_linings.snippet: On this day, in Game 2 of the 1909 World Series, Ty Cobb stole home base. The details around this famous of all capers are what make it so. Losing Game 1 to the Pittsburgh Pirates, Detroit Tiger’s star and all-time great Ty Cobb was sitting on third base at the top of the second […]
global_silver_linings.reason: History is full of quiet turning points and acts of courage that shaped a better world — pausing to remember them reminds us that progress, however slow, is real and cumulative.

global_silver_linings.title: Three surprising reasons to slow down for a thoughtful, nutritious breakfast
global_silver_linings.snippet: From cognitive function to reinforcing family bonds, the benefits of making time for good, whole foods in the morning are plentiful
global_silver_linings.reason: Small daily rituals like a proper breakfast turn out to carry surprising benefits for body and mind, a gentle reminder that caring for ourselves doesn't have to be complicated or costly.

global_silver_linings.title: How a youth group of Cherokee girls made history fighting for a sacred river
global_silver_linings.snippet: What started as an afternoon of river tubing turned into a historic legal campaign.
global_silver_linings.reason: A group of Cherokee girls took on the fight to protect a sacred river and made history doing it — proof that young people rooted in their culture and community can be a powerful force for the natural world.

global_silver_linings.title: Gen Z Is Rescuing Millions in Medical Supplies
global_silver_linings.snippet: In early August, a freight truck pulled up to an OhioHealth facility in Columbus and took roughly 30,000 pounds of N95 masks and hot-and-cold packs, all boxed, sealed and stamped with expiration dates still a year or two out. Left alone, the estimated $250,000 worth of medical supplies would eventually...
global_silver_linings.reason: Gen Z is redirecting millions of dollars' worth of unused medical supplies to people who need them most, turning waste into care through sheer resourcefulness and determination.

global_silver_linings.title: The floating scarecrow saving seabirds from fishing nets
global_silver_linings.snippet: BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM A bird-shaped kite and a floating scarecrow with spinning eyes reduced seabird deaths in Cornish fishing nets by up to 71 percent in a two-year trial. The devices cost relatively little, don’t require significant changes to how fishers work, and are already on the market. An estimated 95,000 diving […] The post The floating scarecrow saving seabirds from fishing nets first appeared on The Optimist Daily: Making Solutions the News .
global_silver_linings.reason: A simple, low-tech floating scarecrow is sparing seabirds from deadly fishing nets, showing that protecting wildlife sometimes just takes an observant mind and a willingness to try something new.

discovery_articles.title: Oculus Tower in Ferrara, Italy
discovery_articles.snippet: At first glance, the Oculus Tower looks more like a futuristic arena than part of an old distillery. Rising from the remains of the former Eridania industrial complex in Ferrara, this seven-story circular concrete structure was once the heart of a large alcohol-production plant. The tower's most striking feature is its enormous open center.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: What was once a roaring alcohol-production engine now stands as a hollow concrete colossus — seven stories of industrial ghost, its open center gaping at the sky like an eye that outlived its purpose. There's something quietly haunting about beauty that was never meant to be beautiful.

discovery_articles.title: Museo Torre del Vino in Socuéllamos, Spain
discovery_articles.snippet: In Socuéllamos, you can climb a tower without ever leaving the world of wine. The Museo Torre del Vino occupies the town’s former railway station, but its most eye-catching feature is the improbable tower rising above it—a vertical tribute to the grape in the heart of La Mancha. Opened in 2014, the museum explores Socuéllamos’s long relationship with viticulture, from grape cultivation and traditional winemaking to the science and rituals of tasting.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Only in La Mancha would someone plant a wine tower inside a decommissioned railway station — as if the grapes needed a grander departure point than the trains ever did. Don Quixote would have approved.

discovery_articles.title: Flu Season Started Early in Parts of the U.S., and Experts Say You Should Consider Getting the Seasonal Jab ASAP. Here's What to Know
discovery_articles.snippet: The season usually starts in October or November. But some western states, including California, Washington, Alaska and Hawaii, began seeing a rise in flu cases as early as August
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Flu arriving in August in Hawaii and Alaska isn't just early — it's a quiet signal that the seasonal rhythms we've long relied on are quietly shifting beneath us. Consider the calendar unreliable, and your pharmacist a new kind of oracle.

discovery_articles.title: Thieves Pulled Off Another Shocking Art Heist in France. This Time, They Took a 330-Pound Bronze Book Cover Designed by Salvador Dalí
discovery_articles.snippet: The volume, "Livre de l’Apocalypse," was a "masterpiece" collaboration of 14 artists and writers. It is one of the heaviest and most expensive books ever made
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Somewhere in France, thieves hauled away 330 pounds of Dalí-touched bronze — a book, of all things, co-created by 14 artists and worth a small fortune — which somehow feels like exactly the kind of surrealist crime Dalí himself might have scripted. The audacity is almost an homage.

discovery_articles.title: African Elephants Often Produce Choruses of Low-Pitched Rumbles. Now, Scientists Are Using A.I. to Decode the Joint Vocalizations
discovery_articles.snippet: New research suggests the animals' overlapping calls serve as coordinated group messages and may contain additional information beyond what’s encoded in individual rumbles
discovery_articles.ferns_note: African elephants aren't just calling to each other — they may be harmonizing in ways that carry meaning greater than the sum of their individual voices, a kind of communal sentence no single animal could utter alone. It reframes the rumble of a herd as something closer to a chorus.

discovery_articles.title: From Slasher Films to Vampire Flicks, Horror Movies Are More Popular Than Ever. Relive the Genre's Scariest Moments—if You Dare—at a New Exhibition
discovery_articles.snippet: The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures' latest show features nearly 350 props, costumes and artifacts from such films as "Psycho," "The Shining" and "Sinners"
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Nearly 350 objects from horror's most iconic films gathered under one roof means the knife from *Psycho* and the carpet from *The Shining* are finally, uncomfortably, neighbors. Sometimes the most unsettling thing about horror is how lovingly we preserve it.

featured_read.title: If You Want a Real Digital Commons, Build It Yourself
featured_read.snippet: Rappler’s answer to state-sponsored lies and harassment was to stop using corporate social media as its public square.
featured_read.blurb: When a Philippine newsroom became a target of coordinated disinformation, it didn't fight the algorithm — it abandoned the platform entirely and built something harder to silence. This is the quietly radical story of what a genuine digital commons might actually require.

reading_room.title: Anne Carson’s Seductive Strangeness
reading_room.snippet: The winner of this year’s Nobel Prize in Literature makes ancient texts feel tantalizingly new.
reading_room.blurb: Anne Carson has spent decades doing something most writers wouldn't dare: making Sappho and Sophocles feel like they were written for the exact loneliness you're feeling right now. A consideration of what it means to win the Nobel for work that has always resisted easy explanation.

reading_room.title: Barbara Ward’s vision
reading_room.snippet: She was among the first to argue that prosperity, equality and the protection of nature are inseparable planetary goals - by Or Rosenboim Read on Aeon
reading_room.blurb: Decades before sustainability became a buzzword, economist Barbara Ward was already arguing that you cannot separate a thriving economy from a thriving planet — and the world's measured, belated arrival at her conclusions is its own kind of indictment. A rescue of a visionary mind from undeserved obscurity.

reading_room.title: Our Ancient Ancestors’ Lost Habitat Revealed by 700,000-Year-Old Elephant’s Tooth
reading_room.blurb: A single fossilized elephant tooth has quietly rewritten the map of where our deep ancestors lived, revealing a green, wet world that shaped human prehistory in ways we're only beginning to reconstruct. The kind of discovery that makes deep time feel suddenly, vertiginously close.

reading_room.title: How to ignite your creativity
reading_room.snippet: Turn a mistake into art, write your own postcard: crafty ideas to escape the doom-scroll and jumpstart your creative practice - Video by Struthless Watch on Psyche
reading_room.blurb: Rather than offering abstract advice about creativity, this piece hands you small, concrete provocations — turning a mistake into something made, sending yourself a postcard from nowhere — that treat the creative rut as a door rather than a wall.

reading_room.title: Making of a Poem: Natalie Shapero on “The Top of Hell”
reading_room.snippet: For our series Making of a Poem, Natalie Shapero talks about her issue no. 257 poem, “The Top of Hell.”
reading_room.blurb: Natalie Shapero pulls back the curtain on how a poem called 'The Top of Hell' came to exist, and in doing so reveals the strange, oblique thinking that separates a finished poem from the anxious notes that precede it. A rare look at the exact moment a piece of language finds its nerve.

garden_note.note: The garden is settling into its amber quietude tonight, Zürich — dahlias are making their final bow and the last of the quince hang like lanterns against bare branches. It's the kind of October evening that asks you to light something warm indoors and feel quietly grateful for every bulb you managed to tuck in before the cold had its full say.
in_season: Quince — harvest before the first hard frost
Dahlias — lift and store tubers as nights dip toward zero
Spinach & lamb's lettuce — sow or harvest cold-hardy leaves
Rake and compost fallen leaves for next year's mulch
garden_note.sky_tonight: With the crescent moon almost dark, tonight's inky sky over Zürich is perfect for spotting the Pleiades rising in the east — look for that soft silver smudge in Taurus after 21:00.
garden_note.sun_times: First light crept in at 07:05 this morning, and dusk folded the garden away at 19:20 tonight.

puzzle.prompt:
I gather light but hold no flame,
I shrink with cold yet bear no pain,
By morning I have slipped away —
I only live at close of day.
puzzle.hint: Think of what you are sitting in right now, as you read this.

fern_data.greeting: A floating scarecrow is out on the open water right now, quietly saving seabirds from fishing nets — and somehow that pairs perfectly with David Byrne setting Elon Musk quotes to music. Both are, in their way, absurdist problem-solving.
